name: Avocado
summary: Avocados are a creamy, high-fat fruit eaten raw, mashed or sliced. This page lists what people say avocados do; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: Avocado is rich in monounsaturated fat, fibre and plant compounds, according to a 2025 review of reviews.

The UK food table (CoFID) measures the flesh of a Hass avocado at 171 kcal, 17.4 g of fat (4.15 g saturated), 3.1 g of fibre, 583 mg of potassium, 2.19 mg of vitamin E and 31 µg of folate per 100 g. It does not measure carotenoids or most plant compounds.
In lab digestion tests of Hass avocado, fat-soluble compounds such as carotenoids and tocopherols were released from the fruit, and fatty acids more readily than carotenoids and tocopherols.
A 2025 evidence map found that avocado trials used 60 to 300 g a day, far more than the 0 to 10 g a day typical in the observational studies.

tableFoods.label: Half a Hass avocado, flesh only (about 80 g)

processing: Ripeness matters in the lab: a study that digested Hass avocado pulp at five ripening stages found that how much of the fat-soluble compounds were released depended on the ripening stage.
Varieties differ: the UK food table lists 17.4 g of fat per 100 g in Hass flesh and 19.3 g in Fuerte flesh.

whoShouldBeCareful.note: In a 1999 study, more than half of people with latex allergy were sensitised to avocado, and about 10 to 20 percent reported reactions after eating it. If you have a latex allergy, talk to your doctor or an allergist.

The UK food table lists 583 mg of potassium per 100 g of Hass avocado flesh. A 2018 review says a dietary potassium limit is usually recommended for people with reduced kidney function. If you have kidney disease, talk to your doctor or dietitian.

unknowns: Whether eating avocado changes blood fats: a 2025 meta-analysis of 10 randomised trials found no significant change in triglycerides, total cholesterol or HDL cholesterol, while a 2025 umbrella review of eight reviews reported lower LDL cholesterol in people with abnormal blood fats. The reviews disagree.
Whether trial results carry over to ordinary eating: trials used 60 to 300 g of avocado a day, and observational studies far less.
What the seed does: this page does not review avocado seed.
